notes: MCP TOOLS. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: implement `Tool` for each tool (`def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema: same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions and required list), and expose `pub fn register(registry: &mut ToolRegistry)` from lib.rs. Output text must equal the TypeScript's: same wording, same JSON shape and key order (serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate, keep it). State the TypeScript keeps in module variables goes in a struct fetched with `ctx.state::<T>()`. Page access is only through `ctx.browser` (the `Browser` trait: evaluate, cookies, set_cookie, delete_cookie, add_init_script, remove_init_script, screenshot, input, viewport, page): where the TypeScript uses Chrome DevTools Protocol calls or Electron APIs, use the matching method, and prefer doing the work with JavaScript through `evaluate` when the page itself can answer (localStorage and sessionStorage, DOM edits, service worker registrations via navigator.serviceWorker). When nothing matches (native dialog handling, download tracking, response overrides, vision model calls that need an API client), do NOT edit rever-tools-api: keep the tool registered with its full schema and validation, return `utils::err(tool::unsupported("<what>"))` from that path, and list the missing capability under behaviorDifferences in your report. Scripts to inject are already ported in rever-inject. Async: `call` returns a boxed future run on a tokio runtime; tests use #[tokio::test] and a fake `Browser` written in the test module that records calls and returns canned JSON. A tool file gets the `Port of` marker when all of its tools are registered.
